claim: All datetime operations use naive datetime.now() with no timezone. _parse_relative() computes offset timestamps in system local time, and _parse_absolute() uses replace() on naive datetime which can silently produce wrong wall-clock times when the system timezone differs from IST. The server may run in UTC while AND9 targets IST (Asia/Kolkata).
evidence: time_parser.py:184 now = datetime.now(); 256 now = datetime.now(); 257 trigger = now.replace(hour=hour, minute=minute, second=0, microsecond=0). All three calls produce naive datetimes. The replace() on line 257 discards any timezone the user intends (IST) and uses whatever the system local timezone reports, which for a cloud server is typically UTC. The past-check on line 261 (trigger <= now) compares two naive datetimes that may be in different semantic timezones.
runtimeTrigger: Server running in UTC. User says 'set alarm 10 PM' at 4 PM UTC (9:30 PM IST). now = 16:00 UTC, replace(hour=22) → 22:00 UTC same day. since 22:00 > 16:00, day_offset stays 0. But user meant 10 PM IST = 16:30 UTC, which has ALREADY PASSED at 16:00 UTC. Alarm fires 6 hours late.

claim: _execute_fallback() hardcodes a subset of 11 cities for city-time lookup, excluding all 16+ smaller cities that timezone_utils supports (ahmedabad, pune, jaipur, lucknow, chandigarh, bhopal, indore, kochi, nagpur, patna, surat, bhubaneswar, guwahati, amritsar, varanasi, agra). Users asking for time in these cities get the generic system time instead of IST.
evidence: reflex.py:514 calls detect_city_time_query(query) which correctly identifies any supported city. Lines 515-518 then checks if the returned city is in a hardcoded tuple of only 11 cities (kolkata, calcutta, delhi, new delhi, dilli, mumbai, bombay, chennai, madras, bangalore, bengaluru, hyderabad). Cities like 'pune', 'jaipur', 'lucknow' pass detect_city_time_query() but fail the hardcoded check and fall through to line 528-530 which returns `datetime.now()` (generic local time).
runtimeTrigger: User says 'pune time' or 'jaipur ka time'. Reflex brain matches TIME action. _execute_fallback is called. detect_city_time_query('pune time') returns 'pune'. City 'pune' is NOT in hardcoded tuple on lines 515-518. Falls through to line 528: returns 'Current time is <system_local_time>' instead of 'In Pune, it's <IST_time>'.

claim: os.makedirs() on line 37 runs at module import time with a hardcoded default path '/app/.jarvis_data/reminders.db'. If the directory /app/ does not exist, this raises FileNotFoundError which crashes the module import because it is NOT wrapped in a try-except block. Only init_db() is wrapped at lines 205-208.
evidence: reminders/db.py:31-37 _DB_PATH = os.environ.get('AND9_REMINDERS_DB', '/app/.jarvis_data/reminders.db'); os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_DB_PATH), exist_ok=True). This runs at module import time (lines 31-37 are at module level). os.makedirs with exist_ok=True only suppresses FileExistsError — if parent '/app/' doesn't exist, it raises FileNotFoundError. Import crashes. The try-except at lines 205-208 wraps init_db(), not the makedirs call.
runtimeTrigger: Run on any system where /app/ doesn't exist and AND9_REMINDERS_DB env var is not set. Module import of app.and9.reminders.db raises FileNotFoundError at line 37. Any import of this module crashes the application.

claim: TimerService background worker runs an infinite loop with no shutdown mechanism. While it works as a daemon thread (killed at exit), there is no way to cleanly stop the timer service for testing or graceful shutdown.
evidence: timer.py:134-138 def _run(self): while True: time.sleep(1); self._prune(). No stop event, no Ephemeral flag, no way to signal exit. The __init__ also starts the worker immediately (line 52) which means even get_timer_service() creates a persistent thread on first call.
runtimeTrigger: When a test creates a TimerService, the background thread lives forever. Teardown cannot stop it. Unit tests that create/destroy TimerService instances may leak threads.

claim: Line 78 has a dead/no-op conditional: both branches execute renderTimers() identically. The conditional is always true but serves no purpose.
evidence: timer.js:77-79 if (changed) renderTimers(); else renderTimers(); — both branches call the same function with no arguments. The changed variable is computed but never used to branch differently.
runtimeTrigger: Every 250ms local tick. renderTimers() is always called regardless of state. No behavioral impact but indicates incomplete implementation (likely intended to be 'if (changed) showAlert()' or similar).
